criteria.descriptor: Correctly identifies the failure mechanism (high LR + random-head gradients overwriting pretrained features = catastrophic forgetting; BatchNorm train/eval running-stat drift) and every prescribed technique is technically sound: the freeze/fine-tune decision, low/discriminative LRs, BN eval() vs requires_grad distinction, and ImageNet preprocessing. No false claims (e.g., does not assert requires_grad=False freezes BN stats, or that Adam 1e-3 across the backbone is fine).

Addresses all requested facets: the freeze-vs-fine-tune decision, the learning-rate strategy, BatchNorm handling, overfitting AND class-imbalance controls, and leakage-free validation — plus preprocessing and gradual unfreezing — rather than covering only one or two.

Ties each recommendation to the specific constraints (small ~4k imbalanced dataset, real domain gap, grayscale input, the observed train-good/test-bad symptom) rather than reciting generic best practices; explains why, e.g., feature extraction and low LR follow from data scarcity plus a random head.

Presents a clear diagnosis followed by an actionable, ordered plan, using correct terminology (feature extraction, discriminative/layer-wise LR, catastrophic forgetting, BN running statistics, gradual unfreezing, macro-F1) precisely.

expected_answer_points: Diagnoses that Adam lr=1e-3 full fine-tuning is too aggressive: the randomly-initialised head's large initial gradients, at a high LR, backpropagate into and overwrite the pretrained backbone features (catastrophic forgetting), so transfer provides little benefit.

Applies the dataset-size x domain-gap decision: with only ~4k images and a real domain gap, start with feature extraction (freeze backbone, train the new head first / head warmup) and keep the earliest generic layers frozen, rather than fine-tuning everything at once.

Prescribes discriminative / low learning rates — much smaller LR for pretrained layers (~1e-4 to 1e-5) than for the head — with warmup and decay, and prefers SGD+momentum or AdamW with weight decay over Adam at 1e-3.

Handles BatchNorm correctly: a frozen backbone must be in eval() so BN uses the frozen ImageNet running statistics (and dropout is off); notes that requires_grad=False alone does NOT stop BN running-stat updates, and that BN stat drift on small/imbalanced batches explains the train-good/test-bad gap.

Controls overfitting and imbalance on the small set: domain-appropriate augmentation, weight decay/dropout, early stopping, label smoothing, and class-weighted loss or resampling for the 6-class imbalance.
Uses gradual unfreezing (ULMFiT-style / slanted LRs), unfreezing top blocks first, to avoid destroying generic low-level features.
Fixes input preprocessing to match pretraining: ImageNet normalisation, replicating grayscale to 3 channels, and matching resize/crop.

Specifies leakage-free evaluation: stratified split by physical part/lot (not by image crop), a held-out test set representative of deployment, macro-F1/per-class metrics instead of raw accuracy, and a frozen-feature baseline compared against fine-tuning.
common_pitfalls: Prescribes 'just fine-tune the whole network' but only tweaks epochs — never lowers the LR or warms up the head — missing that the random head's gradients at lr=1e-3 are what destroy the pretrained features.
Attributes the train-good/test-bad gap purely to overfitting and overlooks the BatchNorm running-statistic train/eval mismatch (or wrongly assumes requires_grad=False also freezes BN stats).
Says to freeze the backbone but leaves it in .train() mode, or conflates requires_grad=False with .eval(), so BN running stats and dropout still change behaviour on the new domain.
Recommends raw accuracy as the validation metric on an imbalanced 6-class problem, ignoring class weighting/macro-F1 and per-class recall.
Ignores data leakage in the split — multiple crops/views of the same physical part landing in both train and test — which inflates validation numbers and hides poor generalisation.

Forgets that inputs must match pretraining: no ImageNet normalisation, no grayscale-to-3-channel replication, or applies augmentations (flips/rotations) that change the semantics of directional defects.
reference_answer:
Diagnosis. Two things break the plan. (1) The new head is randomly initialised, so on the first batches it produces a large loss and large gradients; at Adam lr=1e-3 those gradients flow straight into the pretrained backbone and overwrite the ImageNet features transfer was supposed to reuse (catastrophic forgetting). With only ~4k images the network then memorises the training set. (2) The 'val high early, then degrades / poor test' pattern is the classic BatchNorm + overfitting signature. If the backbone were frozen via requires_grad=False but left in .train() mode, its BN layers keep updating running_mean/running_var from small, imbalanced target batches and dropout stays active, creating a train/eval mismatch. Crucially, requires_grad=False stops weight updates but does NOT stop BN running-stat updates — only module.eval() does.

Strategy (ordered):
1. Preprocessing must match pretraining: resize/crop to the model's expected input, replicate the single grayscale channel to 3 channels, and normalise with the ImageNet mean/std the backbone was trained on.
2. Freeze-vs-fine-tune: with ~4k images and a genuine domain gap, start with feature extraction — freeze the backbone, put it in eval() so BN uses the frozen ImageNet statistics, attach the new head, and train only the head to convergence (head warmup). This is a strong, cheap baseline that cannot wreck the backbone.
3. Then fine-tune gradually: unfreeze the top residual block(s) and use discriminative learning rates — a small LR for the backbone (~1e-4 to 1e-5) and a higher one for the head — with warmup and cosine/step decay. Prefer SGD+momentum or AdamW with weight decay over Adam at 1e-3. Use gradual (ULMFiT-style) unfreezing of deeper blocks only if data supports it; keep the earliest generic layers frozen given data scarcity.
4. Overfitting/imbalance: strong but semantically-safe augmentation (avoid flips/rotations that change a directional defect), weight decay, head dropout, label smoothing, early stopping, and a class-weighted loss or resampling for the 6-class imbalance.
5. Evaluation: use a leakage-free stratified split — split by physical part/lot so crops of the same part never span train and test — monitor macro-F1/per-class recall rather than raw accuracy, and compare the frozen-feature baseline against the fine-tuned model on a held-out test set representative of deployment.
